heading: Learn Modern Standard Arabic, from the script to C1.
lead: A complete course in الفصحى, the written and formal spoken standard of the Arab world. It starts with the letters and their joined forms, teaches roots, patterns, the cases and the ten verb forms directly, and ends with media Arabic, registers and literature. Vowel signs are shown at first and left out step by step, as in real print.
fineprint: The whole course is free: all 77 modules, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test. Specializations, stories, conversation practice, CIMA practice papers and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course: eight tiers, 77 modules

items.title: Tier 1 · Script and sounds
items.text: The letters and their joined forms, the sounds English lacks, vowel signs, the article.

items.title: Tier 2 · First sentences
items.text: Gender, the iḍāfa, attached pronouns, the perfect and the imperfect.

items.title: Tier 3 · The root and the cases
items.text: Roots and patterns, plurals, the dual, case endings, hollow verbs.

items.title: Tier 4 · Building fluency
items.text: Verb Forms II–IV, the subjunctive and jussive, comparison, kāna and laysa.

items.title: Tier 5 · Everyday fluency
items.text: Forms V and VI, relative clauses, inna and its sisters, the maṣdar.

items.title: Tier 6 · Intermediate
items.text: Forms VII–X, participles, the passive, conditionals, reported speech.

items.title: Tier 7 · Upper intermediate
items.text: Numbers and counted nouns, formal address, law, business and official Arabic.

items.title: Tier 8 · Advanced
items.text: Media Arabic, registers, Classical Arabic, the dialects, literature.

panel.note: Tiers 1–2 are A1, Tiers 3–4 A2, Tier 5 A2–B1, Tier 6 B1, Tier 7 B2 and Tier 8 C1.

sections.heading: Arabic grammar explained, not guessed at

items.title: The script first
items.text: Tier 1 teaches the 28 letters in their isolated, initial, medial and final forms, the emphatic, pharyngeal and uvular sounds, and how to type on an Arabic keyboard. Transliteration is a temporary aid in Tier 1 only; from Tier 2 on, Arabic appears in Arabic script alone.

items.title: Vowel signs, then real print
items.text: Texts are fully vowelled in Tiers 1–4, partly vowelled in Tiers 5–6, and unvowelled as printed in Tiers 7–8. A setting hides the vowel signs whenever you want to read without them. In the course, every text with a recording is fully vowelled, so the voice reads the right forms.

items.title: Roots, patterns and the verb forms
items.text: The root and pattern system, sound and broken plurals, the case endings, diptotes, weak verbs and Forms II to X are taught in dedicated modules, with the rule stated plainly and examples in Arabic.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Over 5,000 exercises, each answer graded with a reason and a link to the grammar rule. Typed answers are accepted with or without vowel signs.

items.title: Every word inspectable
items.text: Tap any Arabic word for its meaning, forms and audio. The lookup sees past the conjunctions, one-letter prepositions, article and attached pronouns written onto a word, so <bdi lang="ar">للمدرسة</bdi> finds <bdi lang="ar">مدرسة</bdi>.

items.title: Speaking with pronunciation feedback
items.text: Every module has speaking exercises, and what you say is assessed for pronunciation.

items.title: CIMA (Institut du monde arabe)
items.text: Two timed practice papers in the task formats of the CIMA, the test of Modern Standard Arabic that places you on a level from A1 to C2: listening, reading without vowel signs, and the three writing tasks rated by AI against the CIMA criteria. There is no speaking test, and no CIMA level is given.

items.question: Which Arabic does the course teach?
items.answer: Modern Standard Arabic (الفصحى), the standard shared by all Arab countries in writing, news and formal speech. Every exercise, text and recording is in it. The dialects are described in Tier 8 so you can recognise them, but not taught for speaking.

items.question: I cannot read the Arabic script yet. Can I start?
items.answer: Yes. Tier 1 starts with the letters, how they join, the sounds English lacks and the vowel signs, and shows how to type Arabic on a computer or phone.

items.question: Do I have to read without vowel signs?
items.answer: Not at first. Tiers 1–4 are fully vowelled, Tiers 5–6 partly, and Tiers 7–8 are printed without vowels, as Arabic is printed. You can hide the vowel signs at any level to practise reading without them.

items.question: What level does the course reach?
items.answer: C1, over 77 modules in eight tiers. If you already know some Arabic, the placement test tells you where to start.

items.question: Is the course really free?
items.answer: Yes. All 77 modules, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test are free, with 5 Ask AI questions a day. Premium (€8.99 a month or €69.99 a year) adds the specializations, stories, conversation practice, CIMA practice papers and the other extras.
